arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case claims due process bars a prosecutor from judging their own prior decisions.
The state contends general supervisory responsibility does not create a constitutional conflict.
Justice Alito questioned whether signing an indictment alone creates a conflict of interest.
Justice Kagan asked if a pro forma signature is insufficient to require recusal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of judicial impartiality in capital punishment. It determines whether prior prosecutorial involvement automatically disqualifies a judge. The outcome shapes fair trial standards for all criminal defendants.
